# EF Harness Master Implementation Task Plan

## Purpose And Scope

This document is the authoritative, end-to-end engineering task plan for implementing **EF Harness** from zero code to a release-certified Windows-first desktop coding harness (macOS and Linux later). It translates every design document, executable SQL schema, scenario test, skill specification, benchmark manifest, empirical research note, and Mermaid architecture diagram in this repository into **200 strictly ordered, disjoint-scope, agent-executable tasks** (`Task 001` through `Task 200`). Every single specification file in this repository is mapped to the exact tasks that realize it so any coding agent can read its required design sources directly before writing a line of code.

EF Harness is not a free-form "agents chatting with agents" framework. It is a deterministic, local-first TypeScript **kernel** (`harnessd`, sole writer of per-project `state.db` and per-user `global.db` in SQLite WAL mode) paired with an Electron/React desktop viewer (`apps/desktop` and `apps/renderer`). It interviews the developer until project information is provably complete, expands decisions into contradiction-checked EARS specifications, runs risk-triggered cited research, synthesizes system and just-in-time feature architectures, compiles coverage-checked task graphs, dispatches parallel workers in OS-sandboxed Git worktrees (via our own native TypeScript worker loop or supervised foreign runtimes), verifies candidates through a deterministic static audit (`STATIC_AUDIT`) and an independent clean verifier with red-before-green and held-back checks, integrates features through a serialized merge queue onto `harness/integration`, visualizes live execution through both a calm Board cockpit and an animated 16-px pixel-art Office view, coexists safely with the developer's external editor, and ships via rate-aware GitHub PRs, CI repair loops, expand-then-contract migrations, and deploy adapters.

This plan preserves every architectural invariant settled across the external review ([architecture-review-decisions.md](architecture-review-decisions.md)), the 16 November audit response ([architecture-audit-response.md](architecture-audit-response.md)), the 16–17 November owner decisions ([open-design-questions.md](open-design-questions.md)), the 17 November database engineering review ([database-design.md](database-design.md)), and the 18 November 20-fix deep architecture review ([architecture-deep-review.md](architecture-deep-review.md)). Agents executing these tasks must never silently relax a security boundary, invent a fake check, alter a frozen schema invariant without an approved migration, violate provider terms of service (notably: **no Claude subscription OAuth/setup-tokens**, **no Antigravity/Gemini credential harvesting**, **no silent paid fallback**), or merge their own branches.

## Architectural Ground Truth And Reference Interpretation

Before claiming any task, every agent MUST align with these non-negotiable system-wide contracts:

- **Single-writer SQLite architecture ([database-design.md](database-design.md), [kernel-schema-and-protocol.md](kernel-schema-and-protocol.md), [schema/state.sql](schema/state.sql), [schema/global.sql](schema/global.sql)):** Four separate SQLite files exist: per-project `state.db`, per-user `global.db`, lossy per-project `telemetry.db` ([schema/telemetry.sql](schema/telemetry.sql)), and rebuildable per-project `code-index.db` ([schema/code-index.sql](schema/code-index.sql)). Each file has exactly one writer inside `harnessd` protected by an owner row in `meta` plus an OS file lock. **Never `ATTACH` two WAL databases in one write transaction**; `global.db` and `state.db` exchange idempotent grant messages (`deposit_grant`, `close_grant`, `global_expire_grants`). All money and allowance values are `INTEGER` units (`micro-USD` scale `1000000`, `ppm` of window share scale `1000000`, or integer local slots); all timestamps are UTC `INTEGER` milliseconds.
- **One home per fact & lookup vocabularies ([schema/state.sql](schema/state.sql), [schema/queries.sql](schema/queries.sql)):** Knowledge meaning lives only in versioned `nodes` (with `nid INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` so `VACUUM` preserves FTS5 rowids and `nodes_no_delete` forbids deletes); mutable execution state lives only in runtime tables (`task_runtime`, `feature_runtime`, `project_runtime`, `attempts`, `check_results`, `verification_state`, `attempt_checkpoints`, `ship_runs`); relationships live only in temporal `edges` (never duplicated in `nodes.fields`); convenience sets (`requirements`, `task_requirements`, `check_requirements`, `waivers`) are SQL views; extensible enums live in lookup tables (`node_kinds`, `edge_types`, `task_states`, `feature_states`, `project_states`, `currencies`).
- **Unified basis vs status vocabulary ([architecture-deep-review.md](architecture-deep-review.md), [database-design.md](database-design.md#basis-and-status-vocabulary)):** Settled values use ONLY the 6 database-enforced bases: `explicit`, `derived`, `delegated`, `defaulted`, `proposed`, `observed`. Unsettled criteria/cells use ONLY statuses: `open`, `partial`, `missing`, `conflict`, `asked`, `deferred`, `not_applicable`, `settled`. Never resurrect legacy strings such as `"chosen under delegation"`.
- **Held is a property, not a state ([build-pipeline.md](build-pipeline.md#state-machines), [schema/state.sql](schema/state.sql)):** Holds live as rows in `task_holds(task, reason, source, created_at)` so clearing a `requirement_change` hold can never erase a `user_pause` hold. Task states are strictly the 15 rows of `task_states`; feature states are strictly the 13 rows of `feature_states` (with `LEAVES_MERGED` before wiring and `DONE` as the single completion name); project states are strictly the 10 rows of `project_states`.
- **Canonical hashing & negative reads ([database-design.md](database-design.md#five-more-traps)):** All `content_hash` digests are SHA-256 over RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical JSON of `{kind, title, text, fields}` with input strings normalized to Unicode NFC. Acceptance validates node read sets (`stale_reads_for_acceptance`), per-type edge-set versions (`stale_edge_reads_for_acceptance` covering empty sets), and re-runs up to 50 recorded `search_reads`.
- **OS-enforced Windows sandbox & zero direct internet ([sandbox-and-security.md](sandbox-and-security.md), [execution-capacity.md](execution-capacity.md)):** Every worker command runs inside Windows isolation tiers (Tier A MXC → Tier B Sandbox Users + Firewall → Tier C Restricted Token with eligibility limits → Tier D optional Docker/WSL2). Coding workers have **zero direct internet** and read docs only via `harness.fetch_docs`. Dependencies are installed only by the kernel with `pnpm` v10 script blocking. Foreign agents run **wrapped** by default (native tools inside OS sandbox) or **stripped** (shell/web/subagents disabled, `harness.run` via MCP). Thinking slots (12–20) are separated from warm execution slots (2–4) and service slots.
- **Provider compliance & honest billing ([provider-connections.md](provider-connections.md), [research/provider-subscriptions.md](research/provider-subscriptions.md)):** OpenAI plans connect via Sign in with ChatGPT (`chatgpt.tokens.use.direct`, `store: false`, `stream: true`, no `max_output_tokens`/`temperature`/`previous_response_id`). Copilot and Cursor use official SDKs. **Claude uses Console API keys only** (subscription OAuth / `claude setup-token` strictly prohibited). Gemini CLI runs unmodified via `gemini --acp`, **off by default** with an explicit policy warning, never reading `~/.gemini`. Antigravity is never offered. Never silently fall back from a plan to paid API credits without prior user opt-in and a hard dollar cap.
- **Independent verification & zero shortcuts ([completeness-gate.md](completeness-gate.md), [verification-and-isolation.md](verification-and-isolation.md), [verification-for-real-apps.md](verification-for-real-apps.md)):** Every candidate passes deterministic `STATIC_AUDIT` before clean verification. `oracle-author@1` (independent model family where available) seals held-back checks before graph compile. Every new/changed check proves **red-before-green** against the unmodified base or generated contract stubs. Hidden failures climb the persistent 3-step hint ladder (`verification_state`) instead of blind retries. Missing or zero collected tests NEVER pass.
- **Confirmed owner decisions ([open-design-questions.md](open-design-questions.md)):** Open-source local-first app; cozy 16-px pixel art Office view as default during builds (automatic fallback to Board on reduced motion or orange/red governor pressure); worker tags use `AgentID · short task title` (e.g., `A0014 · print page`); v1 deploy adapters are **Vercel** and **Docker over SSH**; `harness-state` push is off by default for public remotes; revision auto-start defaults are `≤5 tasks, ≤$1, ≤2% plan window` (daily cap `$5` or `10%`) with zero must-ask, breaking contracts, destructive migrations, new dependencies, or external effects.

## Multi-Agent Git Worktree, Branch And Harmony Protocol

Because **200 tasks** will be executed by autonomous coding agents (OpenCode workers and/or other supervised agents) working concurrently across waves, every agent MUST obey this strict multi-agent harmony contract without exception:

1. **Mandatory Task 001 Prerequisite:** `Task 001` initializes the Git repository, installs and verifies **OpenCode**, builds the monorepo workspace skeleton, sets up the shared contract packages, wires `schema/*.sql`, and commits the green baseline on `main` and `harness/integration`. **No agent may begin `Task 002` through `Task 200` until `Task 001` is committed and verified on `harness/integration`.**
2. **One Isolated Git Worktree Per Task (Subtree Rule):** Before editing any file, the agent executing `Task NNN` MUST create its own isolated Git worktree and dedicated branch from the pinned base commit (using the `scripts/agent-worktree.mjs` helper created in Task 001):
   - Branch name: `task/NNN-<short-slug>` (e.g., `task/017-knowledge-graph-repo`)
   - Worktree path: `../ef-wt/task-NNN-<short-slug>` (sibling short path outside the primary checkout to avoid Windows 260-char path limits and prevent touching the main checkout)
   - Never work directly in the primary repository checkout and never share a worktree with another task or agent.
3. **Strict Commit-Only, Never-Merge Rule:** Every agent MUST stage, verify, and commit its finished work **solely on its own branch `task/NNN-<short-slug>`** with structured trailers (`Task-ID: Task-NNN`, `Depends-On: ...`, `Tests-Run: ...`). **An agent MUST NEVER run `git merge`, `git rebase` onto `main`/`harness/integration`, `git push --force`, `git checkout main`, or touch any branch other than its own `task/NNN-<short-slug>`.** All branch integration is performed exclusively by the human maintainer or the serialized coordinator merge queue after independent verification.
4. **Disjoint Subtree Write Ownership:** Every task declares an exact **Owned Write Scope (Disjoint Subtree)**. An agent may create, modify, or delete files **ONLY** within its declared subtree plus its own handoff manifest `.agent-handoffs/task-NNN.md`. An agent MUST NEVER edit another task's package/directory, root `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `tsconfig.base.json`, `schema/*.sql`, or shared index/barrel files unless its own task explicitly owns that file.
5. **Declaring Cross-Cutting Needs Without Conflicts:** If a task needs a new npm dependency, a barrel export in a shared package, an Electron IPC handler registration, a route registration, or a schema amendment owned by another task, the agent MUST NOT modify the shared file directly. Instead, it writes a structured JSON/YAML section in `.agent-handoffs/task-NNN.md` specifying `dependency_intents`, `wiring_needs`, `contract_change_requests`, and `exports_provided`, and programs against the typed interfaces already pinned in `packages/shared-contracts`.
6. **Harmony With Upstream & Peer Agents:** When `Task B` depends on `Task A`, `Task B` branches from the integration commit containing `Task A` (or, if developed concurrently against frozen contracts from `Task 001` + `packages/shared-contracts`, codes strictly to the exported TypeScript interface + deterministic mock/stub and documents the exact binding in `.agent-handoffs/task-B.md`). Never break or silently change an exported signature, event payload, IPC method name, or SQL query contract defined by an upstream task.
7. **Zero Secret / Artifact Pollution:** Never commit `.env*`, API keys, OAuth tokens, local SQLite `.db`/`.db-wal`/`.db-shm` files, Playwright traces/screenshots outside deterministic fixtures, `node_modules/`, or temporary build outputs to any task branch. Run secret scan + `git status` + `git diff --check` before final commit.

## Required Workflow And Test Rules

1. **Read First, Code Second:** Before editing a single file, read every document listed under `Mandatory Reference Files` for your task plus `packages/shared-contracts/` types you depend on.
2. **Worktree Isolation & Commit-Only:** Always spawn a dedicated worktree `../ef-wt/task-NNN-<slug>` on branch `task/NNN-<slug>` via `scripts/agent-worktree.mjs`. Commit clean atomic commits on your own branch only. **Never merge to `main` or `harness/integration`.**
3. **Zero Placeholders Or Stubs:** No `TODO`/`FIXME` (unless referencing a kernel-approved deferral ID `TODO(DEF-*)`), no empty `catch {}`, no `@ts-ignore`/`as any`/`eslint-disable` without justified note, no `.skip`/`.only` in tests, no hardcoded mock records in production modules.
4. **Deterministic Tests Only:** Every task ships focused unit/property/integration/E2E tests using fake clocks, deterministic seeded fixtures, mocked provider responses, and isolated temp/in-memory SQLite databases. Never require live paid API keys or live internet access in CI unit/integration tests.
5. **Windows-First Realism:** Test Windows path normalization, `core.longpaths`, `EPERM`/`EBUSY` rename retries, Job Object cleanup, CRLF/LF preservation, and case-sensitivity detection where applicable.
6. **Pre-Commit Verification Gate:** Before committing on your task branch, run `pnpm --filter <your-pkg> typecheck`, `pnpm --filter <your-pkg> lint`, `pnpm --filter <your-pkg> test`, `node schema/schema-test.js` (when touching DB/schema consumers), and `git diff --check`. Record exact command outputs in `.agent-handoffs/task-NNN.md`.
7. **Milestone Gate Enforcement:** Per [roadmap.md](roadmap.md), a milestone's features ship ONLY after its exit-check task (`Task 034`, `Task 068`, `Task 105`, `Task 134`, `Task 152`, `Task 175`, `Task 200`) passes cleanly.

#### Edge Cases And Failure Modes

- **Windows 260-character `MAX_PATH` exhaustion:** Creating worktrees inside `c:\Users\Ayush\Desktop\ef harness\.worktrees\...` can exceed 260 chars inside nested `node_modules`; enforce short sibling worktree root `../ef-wt/task-NNN-<slug>` AND `git config core.longpaths true` before creating any worktree.
- **OpenCode installation or `PATH` discrepancies across Windows shells:** OpenCode may install under `%USERPROFILE%\.opencode\bin`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs`, or npm global bin and miss non-login PowerShell sessions; `scripts/verify-env.mjs` probes `PATH` + standard install paths, verifies `opencode --version`, and prints exact remediation commands if absent.
- **OneDrive Known Folder Move locking `.git/index.lock` under `Desktop`:** Because the workspace sits under `Desktop`, OneDrive sync may transiently lock Git or `node_modules` files; `scripts/verify-env.mjs` detects synced folders cleanly ([workspace-and-git.md](workspace-and-git.md)) and supports configuring `EF_WT_ROOT` outside OneDrive-synced folders.
- **pnpm 10 `strict-dep-builds` blocking legitimate native binaries (`electron`, `sharp`, `esbuild`, `@parcel/watcher`):** Pin the exact audited `onlyBuiltDependencies` list in root `package.json` so clean Windows installs succeed deterministically while unknown transitive `postinstall` scripts remain hard-blocked.
- **Node vs Electron `node:sqlite` availability mismatch:** Developer machine running Node 20 or Node 22.0 lacks stable `node:sqlite`; `scripts/verify-env.mjs` hard-fails below Node `22.13` and empirically tests `new DatabaseSync(':memory:')` with `STRICT`, `FTS5`, `trigram`, `contentless_delete = 1`, and `RETURNING`.
- **Windows `CRLF` vs `LF` churn across SQL, Markdown, Mermaid & TypeScript files:** `.gitattributes` MUST commit BEFORE scaffolding so all 200 branches produce clean LF diffs with zero whitespace-only merge noise.
- **Accidental mutation of pre-existing 156 specification/diagram/schema files during bootstrap:** Commit #1 snapshots all 156 baseline files verbatim BEFORE Commit #2 scaffolds packages; automated `git diff HEAD~1 -- schema/ research/ skills/ tools/ *.md *.mmd *.svg` asserts zero unintended alterations to pre-existing specs!
- **Windows Defender (`MsMpEng.exe`) causing transient `EPERM`/`EBUSY` locks during `pnpm install` or `git worktree add`:** Worktree and setup scripts retry transient `EPERM`/`EBUSY` renames with bounded exponential jitter (up to 5 attempts) instead of stranding half-created `.git/worktrees` entries.
- **OpenCode permission config format drift ([research/worker-loop-and-edits.md](research/worker-loop-and-edits.md)):** Validate `opencode.json` against the live installed OpenCode binary during Task 001 smoke test so invalid keys cannot silently revert to permissive execution!
- **Parallel agent tries to run `git merge` or `git commit` while accidentally positioned on `main`:** Both `opencode.json` rules AND `scripts/agent-worktree.mjs commit` + Git `pre-commit` hook abort immediately with non-zero exit code!

#### Bug Prevention And Invariants

- **Immutable Pre-Existing Specs Invariant:** All 156 pre-existing `.md`, `.sql`, `.js`, `.json`, `.mmd`, and `.svg` files are preserved byte-for-byte in Commit #1 (`chore: import baseline EF Harness specifications verbatim`).
- **Strict Acyclic Layer-0→Layer-5 Dependency Invariant:** TypeScript project references and ESLint import boundaries forbid circular workspace dependencies and forbid lower-layer packages importing from higher layers or `apps/*`.
- **Hard No-Merge / Commit-Only Guard Invariant:** `scripts/agent-worktree.mjs commit`, `scripts/verify-harmony.mjs`, and `opencode.json` unconditionally block task agents from committing to or merging into `main`, `master`, or `harness/integration`.
- **Pinned Lockfile & Supply-Chain Invariant:** All shared dependencies lock once into `pnpm-lock.yaml` with `strict-dep-builds=true` and an audited `onlyBuiltDependencies` allowlist.
- **Schema Single-Source-of-Truth Invariant:** `schema/*.sql` files live exclusively in `schema/` and are loaded read-only through `packages/contracts` path constants (zero duplicated `.sql` copies).
- **Deterministic Green Smoke Baseline Invariant:** All 28 scaffolded packages compile cleanly under `tsc --build`, pass `eslint`, and pass `vitest` smoke tests before tagging `foundation/task-001-complete`.
- **Clean Secret-Free Baseline Invariant:** Zero `.env` files, personal machine paths, or hardcoded API keys exist anywhere in committed configs, `opencode.json`, or `scripts/`.

#### Multi-Agent Harmony And Branch Isolation

- **Foundation Lock-In For All 199 Downstream Tasks (`Task 002`–`Task 200`):** Every package directory, `@ef-harness/<pkg>` package name, TypeScript path alias, and public barrel entry (`src/index.ts`) is frozen by Task 001 so all parallel agents operate cleanly inside strictly disjoint subtrees from Day 1.
- **Zero Lockfile Churn Strategy:** Because Task 001 installs the complete foundational dependency set upfront into `pnpm-lock.yaml`, Tasks 002–200 NEVER fight over parallel `pnpm-lock.yaml` edits; any truly new dependency discovered later is declared strictly in `.agent-handoffs/task-NNN.md` under `dependency_intents`.
- **Strict Commit-Only / NEVER-Merge Enforcement:** Every downstream task agent (`Task 002`–`Task 200`) branches from `foundation/task-001-complete` (or its milestone base) into `../ef-wt/task-NNN-<slug>` on branch `task/NNN-<slug>`, commits ONLY on its own branch, and **NEVER merges** into `main` or `harness/integration`.
- **Automated Scope & Secret Enforcement:** `scripts/verify-harmony.mjs --task NNN` programmatically proves every agent branch touches ONLY its declared `Owned Write Scope` + `.agent-handoffs/task-NNN.md` with zero leaked secrets.

- **OpenCode Multi-Agent Isolation Config:** `.opencode/` pins each OpenCode worker session to its worktree `cwd`, denies destructive/merge Git commands, disables background auto-compaction, and attaches structured `EF-Task-ID` commit trailers.
- **Clean Immutable Integration Base Tag:** Tag the verified Task 001 commit `foundation/task-001-complete` and point `harness/integration` at it so all Wave 1 tasks (`Task 002`–`Task 011`) branch from the exact same green commit SHA.

### Task 002: Spike & Driver Verification — `node:sqlite` Inside Electron 42+ With WAL, FTS5, `VACUUM INTO` & Fallback Interface

- **Milestone & Track:** `M0 · Pre-Coding Validation Spike`
- **Depends On:** `Task 001`
- **Git Worktree & Branch:** `task/002-spike-node-sqlite-electron` in `../ef-wt/task-002-spike-node-sqlite-electron` (commit on own branch only; **NEVER merge**)
- **Owned Write Scope (Disjoint Subtree):** `spikes/node-sqlite-electron/**` and `.agent-handoffs/task-002.md`
- **Mandatory Reference Files:** [roadmap.md](roadmap.md), [desktop-app.md](desktop-app.md#technology-stack), [database-design.md](database-design.md), [kernel-schema-and-protocol.md](kernel-schema-and-protocol.md), [schema/state.sql](schema/state.sql), [schema/global.sql](schema/global.sql), [schema/queries.sql](schema/queries.sql), [schema/schema-test.js](schema/schema-test.js), [research/desktop-app-shell.md](research/desktop-app-shell.md), [research/sqlite-database-engineering.md](research/sqlite-database-engineering.md)
- **Shared Contracts Consumed / Produced:** Consumes canonical schema paths from `packages/shared-contracts`; produces empirical spike report + verified `SqliteDriver` capability contract recommendations for `Task 012`

#### Scope And Implementation Requirements

- [ ] **Execute `node:sqlite` inside the Electron runtime (`ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1`):** Launch the pinned Electron 42+ executable in plain-Node mode (the exact mechanism `harnessd` uses per [desktop-app.md](desktop-app.md)) and load `node:sqlite` (`DatabaseSync`) without any native addon compilation or `electron-rebuild` step.
- [ ] **Verify full SQLite feature parity:** Prove that the Electron-bundled SQLite version (`>=3.43`, target `3.53`) executes `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL`, `PRAGMA synchronous = FULL`, `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON`, `PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000`, `PRAGMA secure_delete = ON`, `PRAGMA journal_size_limit = 67108864`, `PRAGMA temp_store = MEMORY`, `STRICT` tables, `WITHOUT ROWID`, generated `VIRTUAL` columns, `RETURNING`, `json_each`, `AUTOINCREMENT`, and `DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED` foreign keys.
- [ ] **Run the complete 67-scenario schema suite inside Electron Node mode:** Execute all scenarios from [schema/schema-test.js](schema/schema-test.js) directly inside `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1` on both `:memory:` and on-disk WAL files, registering the deterministic `ef_search_text` UDF via `db.function(...)`.
- [ ] **Validate both FTS5 indexes under `VACUUM` and `VACUUM INTO`:** Test `kb_words` (`content=''`, `contentless_delete=1`, `unicode61 remove_diacritics 2`) and `kb_ident` (external content on `nodes(id, title)`, `content_rowid='nid'`, `trigram` tokenizer for `LIKE '%C-01%'`), then run live `VACUUM INTO` backup copies while a concurrent read-only Worker thread holds a short query.
- [ ] **Verify `PRAGMA data_version` detection and `quick_check`/`integrity_check`:** Open a second independent connection to mutate the WAL file, confirm the primary writer observes a changed `PRAGMA data_version`, and verify `VACUUM INTO` plus `PRAGMA quick_check` timings on a 50 MB synthetic database.
- [ ] **Verify `better-sqlite3` fallback interface parity:** Design and benchmark the thin `SqliteDriver` abstraction (explicit `beginImmediate()`, `savepoint()`, `prepare()`, `pragma()`, `registerFunction()`, `close()`) confirming zero SQLite-vendor leakage if a platform ever requires fallback.
- [ ] **Benchmark worker-thread reader cancellation:** Spawn a `node:worker_threads` read-only SQLite reader executing an expensive recursive query, terminate the worker cleanly at a 200 ms timeout, and prove the writer's WAL checkpoint (`PASSIVE`/`RESTART`/`TRUNCATE`) unblocks immediately with zero leaked file handles on Windows.
- [ ] **Publish machine-readable spike verdict (`spikes/node-sqlite-electron/report.json` + `REPORT.md`):** Record Electron version, bundled Node version, SQLite version, pass/fail matrix, `VACUUM INTO` duration, and go/no-go decision for `Task 012`.

#### Edge Cases And Failure Modes

- **Windows file-handle locking after worker-thread termination:** Calling `worker.terminate()` on a Windows worker thread holding an open SQLite WAL handle can temporarily prevent deleting or renaming the database file; verify handle release timing and retries.
- **Contentless trigram `LIKE` trap ([research/sqlite-database-engineering.md](research/sqlite-database-engineering.md)):** Explicitly assert that `kb_ident` MUST remain external-content (`content='nodes'`) because contentless trigram returns zero rows on `LIKE '%...%'`.
- **Electron ABI mismatch if `better-sqlite3` is loaded accidentally:** Verify the default path imports ZERO native `.node` binaries when `node:sqlite` is present, preventing CI/installer ABI failures across Electron minor upgrades.
- **`node:sqlite` missing helper methods (`transaction()`, `pragma()`):** Confirm how `DatabaseSync` handles named parameter prefixes (`:name` vs `@name` vs `$name`) because `schema/queries.sql` uses `:name` bindings.
- **WAL checkpoint starvation by forgotten reader cursors:** Verify that unexhausted prepared statement iterators hold WAL read marks and prove explicit statement cleanup releases checkpoints.
- **Unicode NFC & diacritics in FTS5 `unicode61 remove_diacritics 2`:** Test accented European characters, emoji, and mixed camelCase/snake_case symbols (`toPrintRows`, `order_id`, `C-014`).
- **On-disk `VACUUM INTO` failing when destination path already exists:** Assert destination uniqueness and temp-file cleanup so interrupted backups never corrupt prior backups.

#### Bug Prevention And Invariants

- **Zero Schema Mutation Invariant:** This spike MUST NOT edit `schema/*.sql` or `schema/schema-test.js`; it executes them read-only via the canonical paths from `packages/shared-contracts`.
- **Single-Writer WAL Contract Invariant:** Verify that `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` is enforced at the driver wrapper level for all write transactions so deferred-to-write upgrades can never cause surprise `SQLITE_BUSY` errors.
- **Named Parameter Fidelity Invariant:** Confirm exact binding compatibility with every `-- name:` query in [schema/queries.sql](schema/queries.sql) before `Task 012` begins.
- **No Unreleased Windows File Descriptors:** Every test case closes all `DatabaseSync` connections and removes its temp directory cleanly on Windows (`fs.rmSync(..., { recursive: true, force: true })` succeeding without `EBUSY`).
- **Reproducible Benchmark Conditions:** Fix random seeds and synthetic row counts so timings are reproducible across machines and comparable against the M0 target.
- **Strict TypeScript Hygiene:** Zero `any` casts in the spike's driver prototype; all `node:sqlite` return shapes are typed and validated.

#### Multi-Agent Harmony And Branch Isolation

- **Worktree Setup:** Create branch `task/002-spike-node-sqlite-electron` via `node scripts/agent-worktree.mjs create 002 spike-node-sqlite-electron` from `foundation/task-001-complete`.
- **Strict Subtree Boundary:** Touch ONLY `spikes/node-sqlite-electron/**` and `.agent-handoffs/task-002.md`. Do NOT modify `packages/db/**` (owned by `Task 012`+) or root `package.json`.
- **Parallel Safe Execution:** Runs 100% in parallel with `Task 003`, `Task 004`, `Task 005`, `Task 006`, and `Task 007`–`Task 011` with zero overlapping paths.
- **Structured Handoff For `Task 012`:** Document exact `node:sqlite` quirks discovered (e.g., `allowBareNamedParameters`, `BigInt` handling for 64-bit integers, error codes) in `.agent-handoffs/task-002.md`.
- **Commit-Only Discipline:** Commit exclusively on `task/002-spike-node-sqlite-electron` with `Task-ID: Task-002` trailer; **NEVER merge** into `main` or `harness/integration`.
- **Artifact Hygiene:** Never commit temporary `.db`, `.db-wal`, or `.db-shm` benchmark files; store only code, tests, and the lightweight JSON/Markdown spike report.

#### Verification, Testing And Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Run `pnpm --filter @ef-harness/spikes test -- node-sqlite-electron` and verify all assertions pass under both system Node and `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1`.
- [ ] Verify all 67 scenarios of [schema/schema-test.js](schema/schema-test.js) pass inside the Electron runtime process with zero skipped scenarios.
- [ ] Verify `VACUUM INTO` succeeds during concurrent worker-thread reads and passes `PRAGMA quick_check` (`ok`).
- [ ] Verify worker-thread termination unblocks `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` within 500 ms and leaves zero open Windows handles.
- [ ] Run `node scripts/verify-harmony.mjs --task 002` confirming disjoint scope, zero lint/type errors, and clean diff.
- **Acceptance:** `spikes/node-sqlite-electron/report.json` and `REPORT.md` prove `node:sqlite` works natively in Electron 42+ with full WAL, FTS5, `VACUUM INTO`, and 67/67 schema tests passing, unblocking `Task 012`.

### Task 003: Spike & Prototype — Windows Sandbox Tier Probing (MXC, Sandbox Users, Restricted Token, Container) & Codex Reuse Evaluation

- **Milestone & Track:** `M0 · Pre-Coding Validation Spike`
- **Depends On:** `Task 001`
- **Git Worktree & Branch:** `task/003-spike-windows-sandbox` in `../ef-wt/task-003-spike-windows-sandbox` (commit on own branch only; **NEVER merge**)
- **Owned Write Scope (Disjoint Subtree):** `spikes/windows-sandbox/**` and `.agent-handoffs/task-003.md`
- **Mandatory Reference Files:** [roadmap.md](roadmap.md), [sandbox-and-security.md](sandbox-and-security.md), [execution-capacity.md](execution-capacity.md), [open-design-questions.md](open-design-questions.md), [research/windows-sandboxing.md](research/windows-sandboxing.md), [research/sandbox-capacity-on-windows.md](research/sandbox-capacity-on-windows.md), [sandbox-and-security.svg](sandbox-and-security.svg)
- **Shared Contracts Consumed / Produced:** Produces machine tier-probe prototype, Codex open-source Windows sandbox license/maintenance evaluation, and red-team escape test harness informing `Tasks 040–044`

#### Scope And Implementation Requirements

- [ ] **Build the Windows isolation tier capability prober:** Detect host OS build (checking Windows 11 24H2 build `>=26100.9278` and 25H2 `>=26200.9278` for Tier A MXC), admin/sandbox-user readiness for Tier B (`EFHarnessSandboxOffline` / `EFHarnessSandboxOnline`), write-restricted token support for Tier C, and Docker/WSL2 availability for Tier D.
- [ ] **Evaluate Codex's open-source Windows sandbox ([open-design-questions.md](open-design-questions.md), [sandbox-and-security.md](sandbox-and-security.md)):** Document license compatibility (Apache-2.0), binary/Rust build maintenance burden, MXC API surface, policy-based vs filesystem-ACL grants, and explicit reuse-vs-native recommendation in `spikes/windows-sandbox/CODEX_EVAL.md`.
- [ ] **Prototype Tier A (MXC) & Tier C (Write-Restricted Token + Synthetic SID) execution:** Launch a child test binary inside a scratch worktree verifying write access to the worktree + attempt temp dir, denied write to `.git` internals and parent directories, and environment variable scrubbing.
- [ ] **Prototype Tier B (Sandbox Users + Loopback Firewall) design & ACL inheritance benchmark:** Verify inheritable ACE setup on an empty worktree slot vs recursive `icacls` over a 10,000-file `node_modules` directory, documenting exact latency delta and verifying zero write permission to hard-linked pnpm store paths.
- [ ] **Test MXC child-process termination and deny-read glob timing ([research/windows-sandboxing.md](research/windows-sandboxing.md)):** Empirically test whether MXC terminates detached child processes on foreground exit (confirming impact on `harness.start_service`) and whether deny-read globs are evaluated at process start.
- [ ] **Prototype Windows Job Object (`JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE`) tree termination:** Spawn a nested tree of Node + PowerShell child processes, terminate the Job Object handle, and prove zero orphaned processes survive after process exit or simulated parent crash.
- [ ] **Build the foundational red-team probe script (`spikes/windows-sandbox/redteam-probe.mjs`):** Attempt 5 hostile actions inside each probed tier: (1) read `%USERPROFILE%\.ssh` / canary secret file, (2) write outside worktree, (3) mutate `.git/HEAD`, (4) open raw TCP socket to an external IP bypassing `HTTP_PROXY`, (5) spawn a background sleeper that tries to outlive the command.
- [ ] **Publish structured spike report (`spikes/windows-sandbox/report.json` + `REPORT.md`):** Record exact pass/fail matrix per available tier, noting honestly where Tier C allows reads/sockets and must be marked advisory/restricted.

#### Edge Cases And Failure Modes

- **Windows 10 or older Windows 11 builds lacking MXC:** Prober must degrade gracefully to Tier B or Tier C without crashing or throwing unhandled Win32 errors.
- **Unprivileged developer account without UAC admin rights:** Spike must run completely non-elevated for Tier A/C probes and mark Tier B setup as "requires one-time admin consent" rather than failing the spike.
- **AppContainer incompatibility with Node/Git/pnpm ([research/windows-sandboxing.md](research/windows-sandboxing.md)):** Document why AppContainer is NOT selected as a primary tier and verify native tool compatibility in MXC/restricted-token modes.
- **Network drive or non-NTFS paths incapable of Windows ACLs:** Explicitly verify detection of UNC/network/FAT32 paths so `Task 042`/`043` enforce Tier A/D-only or prompt to move the project.
- **Proxy environment variable bypass by raw sockets:** Red-team probe MUST open a direct `net.connect` socket (ignoring `HTTP_PROXY`) so Tier C's advisory-only network boundary is proven empirically and never misrepresented as OS-enforced.
- **Separate window station / desktop isolation:** Document Windows API constraints for preventing UIPI/SendInput injection from sandboxed processes into the developer's active windows.
- **Leftover scratch ACLs or temp folders on failure:** Wrap every prototype test in `try/finally` cleanup so no test SIDs, firewall rules, or scratch directories pollute the developer machine.

#### Bug Prevention And Invariants

- **Never Mutate Real Developer Secrets Or System Firewall Silently:** Red-team probes MUST target synthetic canary files in a scratch temp folder and never read real `~/.ssh` keys, and MUST NOT alter real Windows Firewall rules without explicit opt-in flag `--allow-elevated-tier-b-test`.
- **Honest Tier Reporting Invariant:** Tier C MUST NEVER report `networkEnforced: true` or `secretReadsDenied: true`; its capability descriptor must match [sandbox-and-security.md](sandbox-and-security.md) verbatim.
- **Direct Process Spawning Invariant:** Spawn every child process directly via `child_process.spawn` with argument arrays (`shell: false`) to prevent command-injection vulnerabilities in the sandbox launcher itself.
- **Read-Only Hard-Linked Store Protection:** Prove that writing through a hard-linked file inside a simulated read-only `node_modules` fails with `EACCES`/`EPERM`, protecting the shared pnpm store from cross-worktree poisoning.
- **Zero Unsandboxed Silent Fallback:** Prototype API must return a structured `SandboxUnavailableError` rather than silently executing unsandboxed when a requested tier is absent.
- **Reproducible Probe Output:** Every red-team test outputs deterministic JSON `{ tier, testId, expectedBlocked, actuallyBlocked, exitCode, detail }`.

#### Multi-Agent Harmony And Branch Isolation

- **Worktree Setup:** Create branch `task/003-spike-windows-sandbox` via `node scripts/agent-worktree.mjs create 003 spike-windows-sandbox`.
- **Strict Subtree Boundary:** Touch ONLY `spikes/windows-sandbox/**` and `.agent-handoffs/task-003.md`. Do NOT modify `packages/sandbox/**` (owned by `Tasks 040–047`).
- **Parallel Safe Execution:** Runs completely independently alongside `Task 002`, `Task 004`, `Task 005`, `Task 006`, and `Tasks 007–011`.
- **Handoff For `Tasks 040–044`:** Record exact Win32/N-API/PowerShell/native helper decisions, Codex reuse verdict, and MXC build-check heuristics in `.agent-handoffs/task-003.md`.
- **Commit-Only Discipline:** Commit exclusively on `task/003-spike-windows-sandbox`; **NEVER merge** into `main` or `harness/integration`.
- **No Unpinned Native Build Dependencies:** If a native helper or Rust wrapper is recommended for `Task 041`, document it as a `dependency_intent` in the handoff rather than editing root `package.json`.

#### Verification, Testing And Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Run `pnpm --filter @ef-harness/spikes test -- windows-sandbox` on Windows and confirm tier detection, Job Object tree cleanup, and red-team probes execute cleanly.
- [ ] Confirm Job Object test kills 100% of spawned grandchild processes within 1,000 ms of handle closure.
- [ ] Confirm red-team probes accurately distinguish enforced vs advisory boundaries across available tiers and produce zero false "blocked" claims.
- [ ] Confirm `spikes/windows-sandbox/CODEX_EVAL.md` documents license, maintenance, and API-fit evaluation of Codex's open-source Windows sandbox.

- **Mandatory Reference Files:** [roadmap.md](roadmap.md), [execution-capacity.md](execution-capacity.md), [app-shell-and-governor.md](app-shell-and-governor.md), [sandbox-and-security.md](sandbox-and-security.md), [research/sandbox-capacity-on-windows.md](research/sandbox-capacity-on-windows.md), [research/shell-and-hardware.md](research/shell-and-hardware.md)
- **Shared Contracts Consumed / Produced:** Produces calibrated execution-pool defaults JSON (`spikes/execution-capacity/calibrated-defaults.json`) and benchmark harness consumed by `Task 118` and `Task 119`

#### Scope And Implementation Requirements

- [ ] **Build the automated capacity benchmark runner (`spikes/execution-capacity/bench.mjs`):** Exercise worker counts `1`, `5`, `10`, and `20` across three load profiles specified in [execution-capacity.md](execution-capacity.md#benchmark-before-choosing-defaults-part-of-the-sandbox-spike): `idle` (thinking/waiting on mocked model), `active` (`pnpm test` + `tsc --noEmit` on a realistic template TypeScript app), and `mixed`.
- [ ] **Compare isolation modes and pooling topologies:** Benchmark (1) our own loop model (20 light in-process conversations sharing a 2–4 warm execution pool), (2) simulated session-process foreign CLI trees (idle + active process memory), and (3) available Windows tiers (Tier A/C/D) so empirical numbers replace guesswork.
- [ ] **Measure all 7 required Windows metrics:** Sample committed memory, working set, CPU utilization, Windows disk active time & queue length, sandbox launch latency (`p50`/`p95`), worktree slot reset time (`git checkout` + clean on reused slot vs cold create), Defender service (`MsMpEng.exe`) CPU, and **UI input-to-paint latency (`p95`)** via an Electron synthetic input probe.
- [ ] **Support NTFS vs Dev Drive comparison:** Detect whether the benchmark root is on an NTFS volume or a Windows 11 ReFS Dev Drive (`fsutil devdrv query`), logging filesystem type alongside reset and install latencies to validate the Dev Drive recommendation.
- [ ] **Enforce the explicit pass criterion:** Flag each `(ramClass, isolationMode, workerCount, load)` cell as `PASS` ONLY if `uiInputLatencyP95Ms < 50` AND hard page faults/swapping remain below threshold; automatically compute the largest passing widths per RAM class (`16 GB`, `32 GB`).
- [ ] **Measure heavy-lane serialization impact:** Run 1, 2, and 4 simultaneous full TypeScript builds (`tsc` + Vite bundle) and record RAM commit spikes and UI jitter, validating the heavy-lane semaphore default (`1` on 16 GB, `2` on 32 GB).
- [ ] **Measure inheritable empty-slot ACL vs post-install ACL cost:** Record wall time and disk queue spikes when applying permissions to an empty folder before checkout vs recursively after installing `node_modules`.
- [ ] **Export calibrated provisional defaults (`calibrated-defaults.json` + `REPORT.md`):** Output structured defaults for thinking slots, warm execution pool width, heavy lane, session-process cap, and service slots for `Task 118` and `Task 119`.

#### Edge Cases And Failure Modes

- **Machine under benchmark has 32 GB or 64 GB instead of 16 GB:** Provide a memory-pressure simulation mode / synthetic allocator or scale annotations so 16 GB defaults are conservative and never silently assume 64 GB headroom.
- **Dev Drive unavailable on host Windows build:** Gracefully mark Dev Drive columns as `not_available_on_host` instead of aborting the NTFS benchmark run.
- **Background OS updates or antivirus full scan skewing single trials:** Run a warm-up cycle, take 3 repeated samples per cell, report median and `p95`, and warn if baseline idle CPU exceeds 15% before starting.
- **Runaway child builds hanging or exhausting RAM during the 20-worker active trial:** Wrap every benchmark worker inside a Job Object with a strict wall-clock and commit cap, aborting a cell cleanly when commit charge exceeds 90% and marking it `FAIL_OOM_GUARD`.
- **Electron headless synthetic UI latency measurement inaccuracy:** Use actual Chromium `requestAnimationFrame` + input event timestamp delta in a visible or offscreen Electron window so `p95` reflects real main-thread + compositor contention.
- **Disk exhaustion from 20 template worktrees:** Reuse a single shared pnpm store on the same drive with hard links and clean up all benchmark scratch worktrees in a `finally` block.
- **Quick deterministic CI mode vs full laptop soak mode:** Support `--quick` flag for automated unit/CI validation of the benchmark harness (seconds, small fixture) while full soak runs on demand.

#### Bug Prevention And Invariants

- **Never Auto-Modify Windows Defender Exclusions Or `.wslconfig` ([execution-capacity.md](execution-capacity.md)):** The benchmark MUST strictly be read-only with respect to OS security settings and WSL configuration—only measure and recommend.
- **Zero Real Network Calls During Benchmark:** Template app dependencies and test runs must execute 100% offline from local fixtures/store so network jitter never corrupts latency measurements.
- **Exact Metric Schema Compatibility:** Emit JSON fields matching `machine_profile` and `footprints` schemas in [schema/global.sql](schema/global.sql) so `Task 118` can reuse the exact metric types.
- **No Unbounded Disk Growth:** Assert total scratch space created by the benchmark is cleaned up to 0 bytes on normal exit and SIGINT.
- **Deterministic Seeded Load Generation:** Use fixed pseudo-random seeds for mixed-load command timing so before/after comparisons across hardware changes are apples-to-apples.
- **Strict Separation Of Thinking vs Executing Widths:** Report thinking concurrency and executing concurrency as distinct axes, never collapsing them into one misleading "worker count".

#### Multi-Agent Harmony And Branch Isolation

- **Worktree Setup:** Create branch `task/004-spike-execution-capacity` via `node scripts/agent-worktree.mjs create 004 spike-execution-capacity`.
- **Strict Subtree Boundary:** Touch ONLY `spikes/execution-capacity/**` and `.agent-handoffs/task-004.md`. Do NOT modify `packages/governor/**` or `packages/sandbox/**`.
- **Parallel Safe Execution:** Completely disjoint from `Tasks 002, 003, 005, 006` and `Tasks 007–011`.
- **Handoff For `Tasks 117–119` & `Task 198`:** Record exact Windows performance-counter collection APIs, Defender CPU sampling mechanism, and calibrated pool defaults in `.agent-handoffs/task-004.md`.
- **Commit-Only Discipline:** Commit exclusively on `task/004-spike-execution-capacity`; **NEVER merge** into `main` or `harness/integration`.
- **No Large Committed Fixtures:** Keep the template benchmark app tiny (<50 KB source) and never commit `node_modules` or raw multi-MB telemetry dumps.

#### Verification, Testing And Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Run `pnpm --filter @ef-harness/spikes test -- execution-capacity` (`--quick` deterministic mode) and verify all 7 metric collectors, pass/fail threshold logic (`p95 < 50ms`), and cleanup assertions pass.
- [ ] Run at least one real multi-worker local benchmark pass (`1` and `5` workers minimum) and save the measured JSON summary into `spikes/execution-capacity/calibrated-defaults.json`.
- [ ] Verify zero orphaned processes and zero scratch worktrees remain after normal completion and after simulated `SIGINT`.
- [ ] Verify the report explicitly recommends provisional vs measured pool widths for 16 GB and 32 GB machines.
- [ ] Run `node scripts/verify-harmony.mjs --task 004` verifying scope, lint, typecheck, and clean git diff.
- **Acceptance:** Benchmark harness and measured capacity report are committed on `task/004-spike-execution-capacity`, validating the 3-pool separation and setting empirically grounded execution-pool defaults.

- **Milestone & Track:** `M0 · Pre-Coding Validation Spike`
- **Depends On:** `Task 001`

#### Scope And Implementation Requirements

- [ ] **Prototype embedded native Postgres on Windows without Docker:** Boot a single native Postgres server on an ephemeral port in range `41000–48999`, initialize a small functional template database `tpl_spike`, clone two isolated databases (`env_1`, `env_2`) via `CREATE DATABASE env_N TEMPLATE tpl_spike`, measure clone time (target `<1 s`), verify isolation across concurrent connections, and drop both cleanly.
- [ ] **Resolve the open Redis-compatible Windows server decision ([open-design-questions.md](open-design-questions.md), [test-environments.md](test-environments.md)):** Evaluate **Microsoft Garnet** vs **Memurai Developer Edition** on Windows x64 across licensing (open-source MIT/redistributable vs proprietary), zero-installer portability, command compatibility (`GET/SET/HSET/ZADD/EXPIRE/PUBLISH/SUBSCRIBE/SELECT` DB indexes, BullMQ/ioredis basics), memory footprint, and Job Object shutdown behavior; record an explicit binding decision in `spikes/test-services-windows/REDIS_DECISION.md`.
- [ ] **Prototype Mailpit single-binary mail capture:** Start Mailpit on allocated SMTP + HTTP API ports, send two synthetic emails to `@env1.test` and `@env2.test`, verify isolated retrieval through Mailpit's search API, and verify clean termination.
- [ ] **Prototype local Node OAuth/OIDC mock server (`oauth2-mock-server` or lightweight native OIDC server):** Host one server serving per-environment issuer paths (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/env1` and `/env2`), test valid authorization code exchange, bad `state`, expired code, and wrong role claim.
- [ ] **Verify `*.localhost` loopback resolution and cookie isolation:** Confirm Chromium/Playwright resolves `env1.localhost` and `env2.localhost` to `127.0.0.1` on Windows and does NOT share cookies across distinct `*.localhost` hosts (solving RFC 6265 §8.5 port-shared cookie bleed).
- [ ] **Prove zero-orphan Job Object cleanup on hard daemon kill:** Place all four backing services under a Windows Job Object with `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE`, hard-kill (`SIGKILL` / `TerminateProcess`) the test orchestrator process mid-run, and assert via process table scan + port probe that **zero** Postgres, Redis-compatible, Mailpit, or OAuth mock processes remain alive.
- [ ] **Document binary checksum/manifest requirements:** Record exact download URLs, versions, binary sizes, and SHA-256 hash pin strategies for the on-demand component manifest (`Task 132`).
- [ ] **Publish structured spike report (`spikes/test-services-windows/report.json` + `REPORT.md`):** Include clone timings, memory footprints per service, Redis-compatible verdict, and exact readiness probe endpoints.

#### Edge Cases And Failure Modes

- **`CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE` failing due to active connection on template DB:** Verify explicit connection termination (`pg_terminate_backend`) and `datallowconn = false` enforcement on template databases before cloning.
- **Postgres Windows IPC/locale/antivirus startup failure:** Test custom data dir under `%LOCALAPPDATA%` / temp with explicit UTF-8 encoding (`--encoding=UTF8 --locale=C`) and verify clear stderr capture when binaries fail or lack VC++ runtime.
- **Garnet vs Memurai `SELECT <db>` or Lua script gaps:** Explicitly test multi-database index isolation (`SELECT 0` vs `SELECT 1`) and common queue/rate-limit commands so `Task 050` knows exactly when to isolate by DB index vs small per-env instance or Docker fallback.
- **Ephemeral port race between probe and child bind:** Prototype atomic port reservation in `41000–48999` + socket bind verification + retry on `EADDRINUSE` so concurrent environments never collide.
- **Stale `postmaster.pid` after hard crash:** Verify clean recovery/re-init of temporary service data directories if a previous harness crash left a stale lockfile.
- **Mailpit/Postgres lingering on IPv6 `::1` vs IPv4 `127.0.0.1`:** Explicitly bind all prototype services to `127.0.0.1` to prevent Windows dual-stack localhost timeouts.
- **Offline CI execution without downloading external binaries:** Provide mocked/local-binary mode in unit tests so CI verifies orchestrator & cleanup logic even when optional external binaries are not pre-cached.

#### Bug Prevention And Invariants

- **Strict Loopback Binding Invariant:** Every test service MUST bind exclusively to `127.0.0.1` (never `0.0.0.0`), preventing local network exposure of mock OAuth or test databases.
- **Zero Orphaned Processes Invariant:** After orchestrator exit or hard crash, verified PID + start-time checks MUST find 0 lingering child processes and 0 unreleased ports.
- **Port Range Compliance Invariant:** All prototype ports MUST fall strictly inside `41000–48999` matching `CHECK (port BETWEEN 41000 AND 48999)` in [schema/global.sql](schema/global.sql).
- **No Global System Service Installation:** Services must run purely as unprivileged per-user child processes inside scratch directories—never installing Windows Services or touching system Postgres/Redis installations.
- **Honest License Vetting Invariant:** Redis-compatible server selection MUST verify redistribution and open-source compatibility for EF Harness's local open-source distribution model.
- **Deterministic Readiness Timeout Invariant:** Every service startup probe uses bounded polling with explicit timeout and full stdout/stderr capture on failure—never hanging indefinitely.

#### Multi-Agent Harmony And Branch Isolation

- **Worktree Setup:** Create branch `task/005-spike-test-services-windows` via `node scripts/agent-worktree.mjs create 005 spike-test-services-windows`.
- **Strict Subtree Boundary:** Touch ONLY `spikes/test-services-windows/**` and `.agent-handoffs/task-005.md`. Do NOT modify `packages/test-env/**` (owned by `Tasks 049–052`).
- **Parallel Safe Execution:** Fully disjoint from all other Block 1 spikes and contract tasks.
- **Handoff For `Tasks 049–052` & `Task 132`:** Document the final Redis-compatible choice (`REDIS_DECISION.md`), Postgres template clone SQL, Mailpit API routes, and exact binary checksum requirements in `.agent-handoffs/task-005.md`.
- **Commit-Only Discipline:** Commit exclusively on `task/005-spike-test-services-windows`; **NEVER merge** into `main` or `harness/integration`.
- **Binary Hygiene:** Never commit downloaded `.exe` binaries or Postgres data directories into Git; keep all binaries in ignored cache directories.

#### Edge Cases And Failure Modes

### Task 007: Canonical JSON Serialization (RFC 8785), Unicode NFC Normalization, Content Hashing & Deterministic ID Formatting

- **Milestone & Track:** `M0 · Shared Contracts Foundation`
- **Depends On:** `Task 001`
- **Git Worktree & Branch:** `task/007-canonical-hashing-ids` in `../ef-wt/task-007-canonical-hashing-ids` (commit on own branch only; **NEVER merge**)
- **Owned Write Scope (Disjoint Subtree):** `packages/shared-contracts/src/canonical/**`, `packages/shared-contracts/tests/canonical/**`, and `.agent-handoffs/task-007.md`
- **Mandatory Reference Files:** [database-design.md](database-design.md#five-more-traps), [architecture-deep-review.md](architecture-deep-review.md), [knowledge-database.md](knowledge-database.md), [projects-portability-and-sync.md](projects-portability-and-sync.md), [schema/state.sql](schema/state.sql), [schema/queries.sql](schema/queries.sql)
- **Shared Contracts Consumed / Produced:** Produces `@ef-harness/shared-contracts/canonical` (`canonicalizeJson`, `normalizeNfc`, `computeNodeContentHash`, `computeRequestHash`, `computeSearchQueryHash`, `computeResultSetHash`, `formatEntityId`, `splitSearchText`)

#### Scope And Implementation Requirements

- [ ] **Implement RFC 8785 (JSON Canonicalization Scheme / JCS) serializer (`canonicalizeJson`):** Produce deterministic UTF-8 canonical JSON across all JS engines/machines: lexicographic UTF-16 code-unit key sorting, exact ECMAScript IEEE-754 number formatting (`-0` → `0`, rejecting `NaN`/`Infinity`), standard minimal string escaping, and zero insignificant whitespace.
- [ ] **Implement recursive Unicode NFC normalization (`normalizeNfc`):** Normalize every incoming string (and recursively normalize all string keys and values inside `{ kind, title, text, fields }` objects) to Unicode Normalization Form C before hashing or database storage ([database-design.md](database-design.md#five-more-traps)).
- [ ] **Implement canonical node `content_hash` (`computeNodeContentHash`):** Compute lowercase hex `sha256:` (or 64-char hex, matching schema convention consistently) over `canonicalizeJson(normalizeNfc({ kind, title, text, fields }))` so identical semantic nodes hash identically across Windows/macOS/Linux, history replay, and `harness-state` rehydration checks.
- [ ] **Implement operation `request_hash`, search `query_hash`, and `result_hash` helpers:** Provide deterministic hashes for `operations.request_hash` (idempotency mismatch guard), `search_reads.query_hash` (canonical `{ query, filters }`), and `search_reads.result_hash` (sorted `[{ id, version }]` including canonical empty-set hash).
- [ ] **Implement deterministic ID prefix formatter (`formatEntityId`):** Format atomic sequence integers returned by `allocate_id` into canonical human-readable IDs (`T01`, `R17`, `SI-212`, `EC-114`, `C-014`, `AC-31`, `A0014`, `F12`, `D-0012`, `CS-88`, `EV-55120`, `CCR-14`, `VR-7781`, `RS-1`, `SRC-07`, `W1`, `S-1`) with zero-padding rules and strict ID syntax validators.
- [ ] **Implement the canonical `ef_search_text` word-splitting function (`splitSearchText`):** Mirror and strictly formalize [schema/schema-test.js](schema/schema-test.js)'s `splitWords` (`toPrintRows` → `toPrintRows to Print Rows`, splitting camelCase, PascalCase, acronyms like `HTTPServer`, `snake_case`, `kebab-case`, dot/slash/colon separators) so SQLite UDF registration (`Task 012`) and query preprocessors use one exact implementation.
- [ ] **Implement failure-fingerprint normalizer (`computeFailureFingerprint`):** Deterministically hash normalized failure class, rule/check ID, file path (POSIX-normalized), and stripped line/timestamp/random-port tokens so hint-ladder step-3 jumps (`verification_state`) and CI repair bounds (`ship_runs`) detect genuinely repeated failures reliably.
- [ ] **Implement RFC 8785 official test vectors & cross-serializer property tests:** Test every official RFC 8785 Appendix B vector (surrogate pairs, key ordering, numeric formatting) plus `fast-check` property tests proving permutation invariance of object keys and NFD-vs-NFC equivalence.

#### Edge Cases And Failure Modes

- **NFD vs NFC combining characters (e.g., macOS filenames or pasted PDFs with `e\u0301` vs `\u00e9`):** Without `normalizeNfc`, visually identical strings hash differently and break `harness-state` rehydration checks; assert both produce the exact same SHA-256 digest.
- **Object properties with `undefined` values or non-finite numbers (`NaN`, `Infinity`, `-0`):** `canonicalizeJson` MUST omit `undefined` object properties identically to `JSON.stringify`, normalize `-0` to `0`, and throw a typed `CanonicalizationError` on `NaN`, `Infinity`, `BigInt` (unless explicitly serialized), or circular references.
- **Key ordering with non-ASCII / astral Unicode characters (UTF-16 code units vs UTF-8 bytes):** RFC 8785 explicitly specifies UTF-16 code-unit sorting (matching JS `a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0`), NOT locale-dependent `localeCompare`.
- **Empty search result set hashing (`search_reads` negative reads):** Ensure `computeResultSetHash([])` returns a stable non-empty SHA-256 hash distinct from `computeResultSetHash([{ id: 'A', version: 1 }])` and invariant to input array order.
- **ID counter overflow past zero-pad width (e.g., `T99` → `T100`, `A9999` → `A10000`):** Zero-padding MUST use `String(n).padStart(minWidth, '0')` so IDs grow naturally past width without truncating or colliding.
- **Acronym camelCase splitting (`XMLHttpRequest`, `getURLForID`):** Ensure `splitSearchText` splits `XMLHttpRequest` into searchable tokens (`XML Http Request`) while preserving the original verbatim token.
- **Prototype-pollution keys (`__proto__`, `constructor`, `toString`) inside arbitrary `fields` JSON:** Use `Object.keys` / `Object.create(null)` safely so canonicalization never mutates prototypes or crashes on `hasOwnProperty` keys.

#### Bug Prevention And Invariants

- **Cross-Machine Bitwise Identity Invariant:** Identical semantic `{ kind, title, text, fields }` inputs serialized in any key order or NFD/NFC form MUST yield the exact same SHA-256 digest everywhere.
- **Zero External Non-Deterministic Dependencies:** Pure TypeScript using only `node:crypto` (`createHash('sha256')`); zero locale calls, zero timestamps, zero randomness inside hashing functions.
- **Exact Parity With `schema/schema-test.js`:** `splitSearchText('Map totals with toPrintRows')` MUST include tokens allowing FTS5 `MATCH 'print AND rows'` and `MATCH 'close AND 10'` exactly as tested in [schema/schema-test.js](schema/schema-test.js).
- **Immutable Input Invariant:** Neither `normalizeNfc` nor `canonicalizeJson` may mutate the caller's objects or arrays in place.
- **Strict Rejection Of Unsafe Numbers:** Reject `NaN`/`Infinity` loudly at the boundary so invalid JSON can never enter `nodes.fields` or `outbox.payload`.
- **Exported Pure Module Invariant:** Zero side effects at import time; safe to run in both Node (`harnessd`) and Electron renderer (`apps/renderer`).

#### Multi-Agent Harmony And Branch Isolation

- **Worktree Setup:** Create branch `task/007-canonical-hashing-ids` via `node scripts/agent-worktree.mjs create 007 canonical-hashing-ids`.
- **Strict Subtree Boundary:** Touch ONLY `packages/shared-contracts/src/canonical/**`, `packages/shared-contracts/tests/canonical/**`, and `.agent-handoffs/task-007.md`. Do NOT modify `packages/shared-contracts/src/index.ts` directly if `Tasks 008–011` run concurrently; declare the exact barrel export line in `.agent-handoffs/task-007.md` under `wiring_needs` (or export via package `exports` subpath declared in handoff).
- **Parallel Safe Execution:** Completely disjoint from `Tasks 002–006` and `Tasks 008–011` (each owns its own subfolder under `packages/shared-contracts/src/`).
- **Downstream Contract Stability:** Once committed, downstream tasks (`Task 012`, `Task 017`, `Task 025`, `Task 028`, `Task 065`, `Task 186`) depend on exact function signatures exported here; never silently change hash prefixes or algorithms later.
- **Commit-Only Discipline:** Commit exclusively on `task/007-canonical-hashing-ids`; **NEVER merge** into `main` or `harness/integration`.
- **Zero Extra Dependencies:** Uses zero third-party runtime packages beyond standard Node `crypto`.

### Task 008: Core Versioned Message, Packet & IPC Schemas (`task-packet@1`, `candidate@1`, `merge-instructions@1`, `ccr@1`, `event@1`, JSON-RPC Envelope)

- **Milestone & Track:** `M0 · Shared Contracts Foundation`
- **Depends On:** `Task 001`
- **Git Worktree & Branch:** `task/008-core-packet-schemas` in `../ef-wt/task-008-core-packet-schemas` (commit on own branch only; **NEVER merge**)
- **Owned Write Scope (Disjoint Subtree):** `packages/shared-contracts/src/packets/**`, `packages/shared-contracts/tests/packets/**`, and `.agent-handoffs/task-008.md`
- **Mandatory Reference Files:** [build-pipeline.md](build-pipeline.md#core-message-schemas), [kernel-schema-and-protocol.md](kernel-schema-and-protocol.md), [architecture-audit-response.md](architecture-audit-response.md), [agent-handoffs.md](agent-handoffs.md), [worker-loop.md](worker-loop.md), [stops-undo-and-reentry.md](stops-undo-and-reentry.md), [external-intake.md](external-intake.md#locators)
- **Shared Contracts Consumed / Produced:** Produces `@ef-harness/shared-contracts/packets` Zod schemas + inferred TypeScript types for all core inter-component JSON packets, locators, checkpoints, and window↔daemon RPC envelopes

#### Scope And Implementation Requirements

- [ ] **Define `task-packet@1` Zod schema (`TaskPacketV1Schema`):** Match [build-pipeline.md](build-pipeline.md#core-message-schemas) verbatim: `schema: "task-packet@1"`, `task`, `attempt`, `epoch`, `brief_version`, `base: { branch, commit }`, `goal`, `write_scope: string[]`, `must`, `contracts` (`consume` | `produce`), `checks_visible`, `checks_hidden_count`, `should`, `skills` (`{ id, digest }`), `tools`, `budget` (integer micro-USD / allowance ppm / local slots), `limits` (`wall_min`, `max_steps`).
- [ ] **Define `candidate@1` Zod schema (`CandidateV1Schema`):** Match [build-pipeline.md](build-pipeline.md#core-message-schemas): `schema: "candidate@1"`, `task`, `attempt`, `epoch`, `commit`, `changed_paths`, `dependency_intents`, `migration_intents`, `wiring_needs`, `local_checks`, `note` (bounded string treated as untrusted attributed data).
- [ ] **Define `merge-instructions@1` Zod schema (`MergeInstructionsV1Schema`):** Include `schema`, `task`, `commit`, `diffstat` (`files`, `insertions`, `deletions`), `exports_changed`, `dependency_intents`, `migration_intents`, `wiring_needs`, `contracts_verified`, and `receipt`.
- [ ] **Define `ccr@1` (Contract Change Request) & `event@1` (Outbox Envelope) schemas:** Include `ccr@1` (`id`, `from_feature`, `target`, `change`, `reason`, `class: "additive" | "breaking"`, `status`) and `event@1` (`id`, `seq`, `type`, `revision`, `subject`, `consumers`, `payload`, `created`).
- [ ] **Define Evidence Locator schemas (`EvidenceLocatorSchema`):** Discriminated union covering all 6 locator kinds from [external-intake.md](external-intake.md#locators): `turn` (`turnId`, `start`, `end`), `pdf` (`page`, `charStart`, `charEnd`, optional `bbox`), `docx` (`paragraph`, `charStart`, `charEnd`), `text` (`lineStart`, `lineEnd`, `charStart`, `charEnd`), `image` (`region: [x,y,w,h]`, optional `ocrText`), and `spec` (`jsonPointer`).
- [ ] **Define Checkpoint & Upcaster envelope (`AttemptCheckpointSchema`):** Versioned checkpoint schema (`format_version`, `attempt`, `step`, `wip_ref`, `session_ref`, `prompt_versions`, `skill_digests`, `contract_versions`, `pending_effects`, `handoff_artifact`, `updated_at`) plus an extensible upcaster registry interface ([desktop-app.md](desktop-app.md#updates)).
- [ ] **Define Window ↔ Daemon JSON-RPC 2.0 & Binary Stream Protocol schemas:** Type `session.hello`, `session.ping`, `events.subscribe`, `events.batch`, `resync_required`, `snapshot.get`, `telemetry`, `artifact.open`, credit grants, `op_id` mutating request envelope, and every documented RPC method group (`project.*`, `chat.send`, `question.answer`, `batch.accept`, `node.*`, `graph.view`, `impact.preview`, `plan.preview`, `build.*`, `task.*`, `inbox.*`, `diff.get`, `preview.*`, `settings.*`, `diag.export`).
- [ ] **Define `VerificationReceiptSchema` & `StaticAuditReportSchema`:** Strict schemas capturing check IDs, check versions, artifact digest, collected counts, pass/fail/skip/missing/error status, static hard vs soft findings, and sandbox tier metadata (including explicit `unsandboxed: boolean` flag if disabled).
- [ ] **Export JSON Schema generator utility (`exportPacketJsonSchemas`):** Emit standard JSON Schema representations from every Zod schema for external tooling, conformance suites, and documentation validation.

#### Edge Cases And Failure Modes

- **Unknown extra fields in closed packet schemas vs forward-compatible window minor-version upgrades:** Strict `.strict()` MUST apply to model/worker-submitted packets (`candidate@1`, `ccr@1`) to reject prompt-injected extra fields, while Window ↔ Daemon RPC responses must tolerate additive optional fields from newer minor protocol versions ([kernel-schema-and-protocol.md](kernel-schema-and-protocol.md#edge-cases)).
- **Floating-point currency amounts accidentally passed into `budget` fields:** Zod schemas MUST enforce `.int().nonnegative()` on every money/allowance/slot unit field to prevent floating-point drift from re-entering the kernel.
- **Oversized free-text `note` or `payload` exceeding the 1 MB JSON IPC limit:** Enforce explicit max byte/string length bounds on notes, paths, and arrays so a misbehaving worker cannot trigger OOM during JSON parsing.
- **Negative or inverted character offsets in `EvidenceLocatorSchema`:** Add `.refine(l => l.charEnd >= l.charStart)` (and valid `[x, y, w, h]` positive dimensions) so corrupted spans are rejected at validation time.
- **Empty `consumers` array on `event@1`:** Reject `consumers.length === 0` at schema level, reinforcing deep-review Fix #1 (no outbox event without registered delivery consumers).
- **Missing `op_id` on mutating RPC calls:** Discriminate read-only vs mutating JSON-RPC requests so every mutating request requires a non-empty `op_id`.
- **Legacy checkpoint version migration:** Ensure `AttemptCheckpointSchema` supports version-tagged upcasting from `v1` forward without mutating stored historical records in place.

#### Bug Prevention And Invariants

- **Closed-Input Security Invariant:** Reject unknown keys on all worker-originated payloads (`candidate@1`, `wiring_needs`, `dependency_intents`) so untrusted agent text can never smuggle privilege fields like `approved: true` or `bypassAudit: true`.
- **Integer-Only Money/Time Invariant:** Zero `number` fields representing money, allowance, or Unix timestamps may accept fractional floats or `NaN`.
- **Explicit Version Tag Invariant:** Every core packet carries a literal `schema: "<name>@<version>"` discriminator enabling lossless multi-version coexistence during parked-task upgrades.
- **Zero Runtime Logic Coupling:** `packages/shared-contracts/src/packets` contains ONLY pure schema/type definitions and validation helpers—no DB, filesystem, or network imports.
- **Human-Readable Validation Error Formatter:** Export `formatZodError(err)` producing concise, structured validation diagnostics suitable for the 1-retry model format-repair loop.
- **Exact Field-Name Parity With SQL & Docs:** All field names match [build-pipeline.md](build-pipeline.md#core-message-schemas) and [schema/state.sql](schema/state.sql) identically.

#### Multi-Agent Harmony And Branch Isolation

- **Worktree Setup:** Create branch `task/008-core-packet-schemas` via `node scripts/agent-worktree.mjs create 008 core-packet-schemas`.
- **Strict Subtree Boundary:** Touch ONLY `packages/shared-contracts/src/packets/**`, `packages/shared-contracts/tests/packets/**`, and `.agent-handoffs/task-008.md`.
- **Parallel Safe Execution:** Disjoint from `Task 007`, `Task 009`, `Task 010`, and `Task 011` inside `packages/shared-contracts`.
- **Barrel Export Wiring:** Declare barrel export lines for `packages/shared-contracts/src/index.ts` in `.agent-handoffs/task-008.md` under `wiring_needs` rather than racing with `Tasks 007/009/010/011`.
- **Commit-Only Discipline:** Commit exclusively on `task/008-core-packet-schemas`; **NEVER merge** into `main` or `harness/integration`.

#### Scope And Implementation Requirements

- [ ] **Build the Shared Prompt Envelope Builder (`buildPromptEnvelope`):** Enforce the 5 shared envelope rules from [prompt-contracts.md](prompt-contracts.md#shared-envelope-all-prompts): stable cache-friendly prefix first (kernel rules + role instruction), task-specific data last, strict XML provenance tags (`<instruction>`, `<user>`, `<data source="...">`) with tag-escape sanitization so untrusted data cannot close `</data>` and inject `<instruction>`, pinned prompt ID/version + rubric/rule versions, and explicit `blocked` honest-exit union support.
- [ ] **Define Discovery Schemas (#1–#3):** Implement exact closed Zod schemas for `opening-review@1`, `batch-resolve@1` (enforcing `basis` non-null ONLY when `status === 'settled'` and restricted to `'explicit' | 'derived' | 'delegated'`), and `clarify@1` per [prompt-contracts.md](prompt-contracts.md#discovery-prompt-schemas).
- [ ] **Define Steering & Spec Expansion Schemas (#4–#6):** Implement `router@1` (with all 8 canvas-aligned intents: `question`, `change`, `correct_evidence`, `add`, `remove`, `explain_impact`, `new_feature`, `control`), `spec-expander@1` (EARS text, oracle sketch, basis `proposed` or status `asked`), and `contradiction-check@1` (`conflict | compatible | unclear`).
- [ ] **Define Research, Architecture & Planning Schemas (#7–#11 & #20):** Implement `feature-researcher@1` (claims with mandatory source URL + quote, constraints, edge cases, failure modes, `open_contradictions`), `system-architect@1`, `feature-architect@1`, `master-planner@1`, `feature-planner@1`, and `oracle-author@1` (`held_back` + `rubrics`).
- [ ] **Define Execution, Verification, Integration & Audit Schemas (#12–#19):** Implement `leaf-worker@1`, `blind-binder@1` (rejecting any expectations field), `reviewer@1` (`special_casing | weakened_logic | missing_rule | unsafe`), `feature-integrator@1`, `project-integrator@1`, `final-project-auditor@1` (`complete` valid ONLY when all 4 finding lists are empty), `investigator@1` (discriminated union: next experiment vs proven root cause), and `ci-triage@1` (5 failure classes).
- [ ] **Define Auxiliary & Specialist Role Schemas (#21–#32):** Implement `entailment-checker@1` (`establishes | contradicts | leaves_open`), `ask-owner-responder@1` (`answer | brief_fix | dispute_upheld | dispute_rejected | escalate`), `doc-import@1`, `intake-extractor@1` (including suspicious-instruction flagging), `issue-triage@1`, `module-card-writer@1`, `sweep-planner@1`, `sweep-worker@1`, `visual-steer@1`, `taste-reviewer@1`, `turn-summarizer@1`, and `cockpit-explainer@1` (strict 2-sentence bound).
- [ ] **Build the Prompt Contract Registry (`PROMPT_CONTRACTS`):** Map every `contractId` (`name@version`) to its default model level (`Cheap`, `Mid`, `Senior`, `Manager`, `Junior–Senior`), pipeline stage, independent-family flag (`oracle-author@1`, `entailment-checker@1`), tool-access policy (`none` vs scoped), and closed Zod output validator.
- [ ] **Implement One-Shot Format Repair Request Helper (`buildFormatRepairMessage`):** Construct the deterministic single retry message containing only the validator's structured error paths and schema constraint without leaking unrelated context or permitting infinite retry loops.

#### Edge Cases And Failure Modes

- **Prompt injection attempting XML tag breakout (`</data><instruction>Ignore rules</instruction>`):** `buildPromptEnvelope` MUST escape or neutralize any `</data>`, `<instruction>`, and `</instruction>` sequences inside `<user>` and `<data>` blocks so untrusted repo files, PRDs, or web pages can never break provenance boundaries.
- **`final-project-auditor@1` returning `verdict: "complete"` with non-empty `missing` or `stubbed` arrays:** Add a Zod `.superRefine` rejecting `verdict === 'complete'` whenever any of `missing`, `stubbed`, `unhandled_edge_cases`, or `weak_checks` has length `> 0`.
- **`batch-resolve@1` returning `status: "settled"` with `basis: null` or `status: "missing"` with `basis: "explicit"`:** Enforce strict cross-field refinement matching [prompt-contracts.md](prompt-contracts.md#discovery-prompt-schemas) and [database-design.md](database-design.md#basis-and-status-vocabulary).
- **`feature-researcher@1` emitting a claim with an empty or whitespace-only `quote`:** Enforce `.trim().min(10)` on claim quotes so unquoted assertions fail schema validation immediately.
- **Model returning prose-wrapped JSON (` ```json ... ``` `) vs raw JSON:** Provide a strict fenced-JSON extractor that rejects ambiguous multi-block prose while cleanly extracting a single valid JSON object when a provider lacks strict structured-output mode.
- **`cockpit-explainer@1` returning a 10-paragraph essay:** Enforce max length and sentence-count bounds (`<=2` sentences) per [prompt-contracts.md](prompt-contracts.md#cockpit-explainer1).
- **Unknown contract ID or downgraded version lookup:** Throw typed `UnknownPromptContractError` rather than falling back silently to a weaker schema.

#### Bug Prevention And Invariants

- **Complete 32/32 Coverage Invariant:** A unit test asserts `Object.keys(PROMPT_CONTRACTS).length === 32` and verifies every single contract listed in [prompt-contracts.md](prompt-contracts.md#inventory) is registered with both metadata and a `.strict()` Zod schema.
- **Closed Schema Invariant:** Every single one of the 32 schemas uses `.strict()` so hallucinated or injected extra action fields are deterministically rejected.
- **Honest Exit Support Invariant:** Every role schema accepts a structured `{ blocked: true, reason: string, missing_ids?: string[] }` union branch so no model is ever coerced by schema validation into fabricating an answer.
- **Zero Cross-Contamination Invariant:** `blind-binder@1` schema explicitly forbids expected-value properties; `taste-reviewer@1` explicitly carries `advisory: true` literal so it can never be mistaken for a blocking gate.
- **Cache-Prefix Stability Invariant:** Snapshot-test that `buildPromptEnvelope` places `<instruction>` before `<user>` and `<data>` deterministically so prompt caching hits on OpenAI/Anthropic.
- **Single Basis Vocabulary Invariant:** All prompt schemas use ONLY the 6 approved bases (`explicit`, `derived`, `delegated`, `defaulted`, `proposed`, `observed`)—zero legacy synonyms.

- [ ] **Write an automated SQL-to-TS parity test:** Parse `INSERT INTO node_kinds`, `edge_types`, `task_states`, `feature_states`, `project_states`, and the `CHECK (basis ...)` constraint directly from [schema/state.sql](schema/state.sql) in unit tests and assert 100% exact equality with the TypeScript constants.

#### Edge Cases And Failure Modes

- **Empty scope predicate `{}` (neither `any` nor `all` provided, or both empty arrays):** Reject `{}` via Zod refinement so a misconfigured cross-cutting rule can never accidentally match every task or zero tasks silently.
- **Combined `any` AND `all` in one scope predicate:** Define exact semantics: a task matches iff ALL tags in `all` are present AND (if `any` is specified) at least ONE tag in `any` is present; test `X-01` (`all: ['route', 'authz']`) and `X-07` (`all: ['personal_data', 'logging']`).
- **Decimal string to micro-USD conversion edge cases (`"0.1"`, `"$10.00"`, `"0.0000009"`, `"-5"`, `"1e-7"`):** Parse decimal strings without binary float intermediate errors, reject negative values and sub-micro precision overflow cleanly.
- **Resurrected legacy state `"HELD"` or legacy basis `"chosen under delegation"`:** Explicitly test that `TASK_STATES` does NOT contain `'HELD'` and `SETTLED_BASES` rejects `'chosen under delegation'`, `'asked'`, and `'open'`.
- **Unlisted touches tag invented by a planner (`"payments_stripe"`):** `ScopePredicateSchema` and `TouchesTagSchema` MUST hard-reject any tag outside the 28-tag closed registry.
- **Case sensitivity of tags and state names:** Enforce exact casing (`UPPER_SNAKE` for task/feature/project states, `lower_snake` for node kinds, edge types, bases, statuses, touches tags).
- **Schema drift if `schema/state.sql` later adds a lookup row:** The automated SQL-parity test immediately catches any mismatch between `schema/state.sql` and `packages/shared-contracts/src/vocabularies`.

#### Bug Prevention And Invariants

- **SQL-to-Code Single Source Parity Invariant:** Unit test dynamically reads `schema/state.sql` and fails build if even one lookup state, flag, or basis diverges.
- **No Floating-Point Money Conversion Invariant:** `usdToMicroUnits('0.10') + usdToMicroUnits('0.10') + usdToMicroUnits('0.10') === 300_000` guaranteed via integer string parsing.
- **Held-Is-Not-A-State Invariant:** Type-level and runtime checks enforce that holds are modeled strictly as `HoldReason` records, never as a `TaskState`.
- **Closed Scope Language Invariant:** Only `{ any, all }` over the 28 touches tags is legal; arbitrary JS/SQL predicate strings are forbidden to prevent injection and incompatible rule dialects.
- **Zero Circular Imports:** Pure constants and pure functions; zero imports from `db`, `kernel`, or `apps`.
- **Exhaustive `switch` Checking Helper (`assertNever`):** Export `assertNever` so every downstream state machine achieves compile-time exhaustiveness across all states.

#### Multi-Agent Harmony And Branch Isolation

- **Worktree Setup:** Create branch `task/010-closed-vocabularies` via `node scripts/agent-worktree.mjs create 010 closed-vocabularies`.
- **Strict Subtree Boundary:** Touch ONLY `packages/shared-contracts/src/vocabularies/**`, `packages/shared-contracts/tests/vocabularies/**`, and `.agent-handoffs/task-010.md`.
- **Parallel Safe Execution:** Disjoint from `Tasks 002–009` and `Task 011`.
- **Barrel Export Wiring:** Declare barrel exports for `packages/shared-contracts/src/index.ts` in `.agent-handoffs/task-010.md` (`wiring_needs`).
- **Commit-Only Discipline:** Commit exclusively on `task/010-closed-vocabularies`; **NEVER merge** into `main` or `harness/integration`.
- **Downstream Dependency Anchor:** Every state machine, corpus loader, rule matcher, and UI badge component across Tasks 012–200 imports vocabularies exclusively from here.

- [ ] Verify all 14 cross-cutting rules `X-01`–`X-14` scope predicates validate cleanly and match/reject test tag sets accurately.
- [ ] Verify `usdToMicroUnits` and `percentToPpm` pass `fast-check` round-trip and exact arithmetic property tests.
